mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) in a walk-forward test.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer payrolls (PAYEMS < INDPRO) indicate weakening labor market strength, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while INDPRO decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) in 3 out of 4 consecutive windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1.5 million units suggests accelerating domestic demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST crosses above 1.5 million units in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is non-positive and the 95% confidence interval includes zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 101.0 for two consecutive months signals supply-side softness that precedes a 20-day S&P 500 bearish skew.
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is not negative in more than 70% of such contraction periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds +2% in a month, it anticipates a tightening cycle that drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in at least 80% of such inflation spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.0% and a rise in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 suggests a strong labor market that precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS > 200000 in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) in 5 out of 6 consecutive windows.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies, so this sketch is invalid - thus we will instead use a demand proxy) - instead, using GDPC1 as a proxy: A 10% increase in GDPC1 from the prior quarter indicates pent-up demand, predicting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is flat or negative with a p-value > 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), the 20-day S&P 500 forward return is uncorrelated with any single macro proxy and exhibits no consistent sign, suggesting regime-specific noise dominates.
failure_condition: In the tightening regime, 20-day forward returns show a mean > 0 with p-value < 0.05 in a two-tailed test over 10 windows.
